definition.simple: The weight of a single atom. It is measured in 'atomic mass units' (u) because atoms are too small to weigh in grams.
definition.academic: The mass of an atom of a chemical element expressed in atomic mass units (u). It is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom.

common_misconceptions: Atomic mass is measured in grams. (Correction: It's measured in 'u'. A single atom weighing a gram would be impossibly heavy!)
ai_context.tutor_hint: Explain that Carbon-12 is the standard 'weight' used to compare all other atoms, like the standard weights used by a vegetable vendor.
